style.vernacular: Flat, green city of five-storey Gruenderzeit (Altbau) perimeter blocks with plastered street facades in ochre, cream and grey and stucco window pediments, steep tile or zinc roofs and inner courtyards; red and yellow brick churches, schools and industrial buildings; monumental 1950s Stalinist ceramic-clad blocks; prefabricated Plattenbau slabs in the east; 1960s-70s concrete modernism; and glass-and-steel post-1990 government and commercial buildings. Cobbled or paved streets lined with lime, plane and chestnut trees; Brandenburg pine forest at the edges.
style.ornament: Gruenderzeit stucco window pediments, cornices and bay windows on street facades; Schinkel-inspired ceramic ornament on Karl-Marx-Allee; brick Gothic and Neo-Romanesque brickwork on churches; coloured panel bands and mosaics on Plattenbau; Lime-tree avenues and cobbled and mosaic-paved pavements.

sources.what: Stalinist socialist-classicist blocks about eight storeys clad in ornate architectural ceramics, Schinkel-inspired; western part has 1967 Plattenbau
17% of buildings Gruenderzeit or older; Plattenbau in eastern Berlin; red-brick Rotes Rathaus; tree-lined Unter den Linden
1930 Neues Bauen stadium, glass-clad iron staircases
